task.title: Track and Finish an In-Progress Operation
task.shortdesc: See the status of a paused merge, rebase, cherry-pick, or revert, then abort, restart, or continue it.

context.p: When an operation pauses because of conflicts, the Git Client shows its current status. The view labels the operation in progress (for example, Merging), and the view marks the related commits with amber labels. Your current commit is labeled Start (Mine), and the incoming side is labeled according to the operation: Incoming (Theirs) for a merge, Cherry-picked (Theirs), or Reverted (Theirs). During a rebase, the commit being replayed is labeled Replayed, and that commit is your own work. A rebase reverses the sides, so your commit is the incoming one. The node is connected by a dashed gray line to its parent commit, or to both parents when a merge is in progress.

The compare editor uses the same labels. Each pane begins with the role of the side, followed by the branch when the commit is the tip of one, the date, the short revision, the author, and the first line of the commit message. The pane you resolve into adds → Resolved. For example, a merge compares Start (Mine) → Resolved with Incoming (Theirs), and a rebase compares Rebased onto → Resolved with Replayed. The window title shows the file name and the operation, for example Merge conflict in config.dita.

fig.title: In-Progress Merge in the Git History View

step.cmd: Resolve any conflicts the operation reported.
Use the buttons in the conflict panel above the file list to finish or back out of the operation. The buttons depend on which operation is in progress:

ul.li: Abort - Restores the state from before the operation started.
Restart Merge - Reverts your working-copy changes so that you can try a different strategy.
Continue Rebase - Completes the rebase after every conflict is resolved.

info.p: After every file is resolved, the panel shows Conflicts resolved and explains the remaining step in its tooltip. It stays visible until you commit, so these actions remain available.
